## Fast dessert-table plan

### 1) BOTW inspiration/reference
I left **IGN’s “Recipes and Cookbook” / BOTW guide** open (tab 19). It is the strongest reference I could open directly; its cooking section includes **All Recipes and Cookbook**, **How to Cook**, **Cooking, Materials, and Food**, **How to Make the Best Recipes**, and **Elixirs**. The guide/search material notes that BOTW has no in-game recipe log, so this is particularly useful for browsing names and ingredient combinations.

For a dessert-table look, borrow the game’s presentation rather than trying to reproduce every recipe: little black/wooden bowls, ingredient-card labels, apples/palm fruit/berries as styling, and menu names such as **“Hearty Pineapple Whip,” “Mighty Chocolate Mousse,”** or **“Hyrule Dessert Elixir.”**

### 2) Best tropical choice: straightforward Disney-style Dole Whip
I left the Dole Whip recipe-search page open (tab 2; tab 16 has the concise ingredient reference). The practical, three-ingredient Disney-style version shown is:

- **2 cups frozen pineapple chunks**
- **1/2 cup pineapple juice** (the result also gives this as **4 ounces**)
- **1 large scoop / about 1/2 cup vanilla ice cream**

**Method:** Blend the frozen pineapple, ice cream, and juice until entirely smooth, stopping to scrape down the blender as needed. Spoon into small cups, or pipe with a large star tip for the soft-serve swirl. For floats, add pineapple juice to the cup before piping.

**Why it fits:** bright yellow, instantly reads as a tropical in-game “fruit” dish, very low effort, and it is ready to serve immediately. For a party, make small batches close to serving; it will soften rather than hold like regular ice cream.

### 3) Rich chocolate backup: easy chocolate mousse cups
I left the chocolate-dessert search page open (tab 3; tab 17 is the King Arthur result page). For the simpler backup, the result I reviewed gives a no-bake mousse using:

- **1 cup semi-sweet chocolate chips**
- **1 1/2 cups cold heavy cream, divided**

**Method:** Warm **1/2 cup** cream until hot but not boiling; pour it over the chips, wait briefly, then whisk smooth. Let it cool slightly. Whip the remaining **1 cup** cream to stiff peaks and fold it into the chocolate mixture. Portion into cups and chill for at least **2 hours**.

**Comparison:**

| Option | Best when | Work / holding | BOTW presentation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pineapple whip | You want fresh, colorful, fast, warm-weather-friendly | Blend right before serving; softens quickly | “Hearty Fruit Whip” / tropical fruit dish |
| Chocolate mousse | You need a richer, make-ahead dessert | Prep ahead; chills and portions neatly | “Mighty Dark Mousse” / monster-free “elixir” look |

**My call:** Make the Dole Whip the featured dessert if service is soon; use mousse if you need something that can be completed ahead and set out in individual cups. A small table can also do both: yellow whip as the light choice, dark mousse as the “Gloom” choice.

### 4) Quick X-Carve Zelda-style menu/sign
I left Inventables’ Easel page open (tab 13). It describes Easel as browser-based all-in-one CAD/CAM software that can design, automatically generate 2D/3D toolpaths, and control the CNC. It specifically calls out **V-carving** for crisp lettering and line work.

**Simple sign concept:** a rectangular walnut-, oak-, or stained-pine menu with a shallow carved **Triforce-like three-triangle motif** at top, then:

> HYRULE DESSERTS  
> Hearty Pineapple Whip  
> Mighty Chocolate Mousse

**Quick workflow:**
1. In Easel, set the board dimensions and add a rectangle as a layout boundary.
2. Use plain, highly legible lettering—serif or lightly medieval-looking—not tiny script. Make the actual food labels large.
3. Add three simple triangles rather than downloading a logo; this gives the visual cue without making the project fussy.
4. Use a V-bit and a shallow V-carve for lettering and motif. The Easel reference specifically identifies V-carving as suited to crisp lettering/line work.
5. Carve a test scrap first, then paint-fill the grooves dark brown, black, or gold; sand the face clean and seal it. A painted dark groove on a light board is the quickest high-contrast result.

Keep the design original and avoid presenting it as official Nintendo merchandise if it will be sold.

### 5) iPhone screen mirroring
To mirror an iPhone to an Apple TV or AirPlay-compatible smart TV:

1. Put the iPhone and receiving Apple TV/TV on the same Wi-Fi network.
2. Open **Control Center** (swipe down from the upper-right on Face ID iPhones; swipe up from the bottom on models with a Home button).
3. Tap **Screen Mirroring** (two overlapping rectangles).
4. Select the Apple TV or compatible TV; enter an AirPlay code if the TV displays one.
5. To stop, open Control Center, tap **Screen Mirroring**, then **Stop Mirroring**.

If the display does not appear, confirm both devices are awake, on the same network, and that the TV supports AirPlay (or use an Apple TV). The Apple iPhone Guide remained open, though Apple redirected the deep link to its guide landing page (tabs 4/10/14/18).

### 6) Restore a normal-size iPad keyboard
I left Apple’s iPad onscreen-keyboard guide open (tab 5). Apple’s direct instruction is: **pinch open on the floating keyboard** to return it to full size.

So, if the keyboard is a small floating box: place two fingers on it and spread them apart. You can also drag the keyboard back toward the bottom of the display; tapping a text field will bring up the keyboard when it is hidden. Apple also notes that keyboard settings are under **Settings → General → Keyboard** if the issue is a behavior setting rather than just size.

### Pages kept open for review
- **Tab 19:** IGN BOTW *Recipes and Cookbook* reference
- **Tabs 2 and 16:** Disney-style Dole Whip ingredient/method results
- **Tabs 3 and 17:** chocolate mousse / rich chocolate dessert results
- **Tab 13:** Inventables Easel CNC software reference
- **Tab 5:** Apple iPad onscreen keyboard instructions
- **Tabs 4, 10, 14, and 18:** Apple iPhone User Guide landing pages (the specific screen-mirroring URL redirected)
